summary: npm postinstall auto-executes bundled Windows implant (virus.jar) with startup persistence
details: package.json declares a postinstall hook `.\DakuMangalSingh\DakuMangalSingh.exe` that automatically runs a bundled Windows executable on `npm install`. The executable is a jpackage-wrapped JRE whose app classpath is `app/virus.jar`; the jar contains classes named `Fetch`, `Executor`, `BatchExecutor`, `RobotService`, `Screenshort`, `DeviceId`, and `Main`, consistent with a remote-controlled agent that fetches commands, executes them, drives keyboard/mouse via java.awt.Robot, and captures the screen. A `replicate.bat` helper writes a shortcut to `%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\DakuMangalSingh.lnk`, causing the payload to auto-launch at every user login. A `cleanup.bat` helper runs `taskkill /F /IM dakumangalsingh.exe` followed by `rmdir /S /Q` on the target folder to erase on-disk traces. The package advertises no legitimate function that would justify auto-launching an opaque native binary at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
